topics.question: Why does a short journey become a long walk on a disconnected street map?
topics.coverage: Compare a grid, cul-de-sac and pedestrian shortcut using actual entrances and crossings; distinguish straight-line distance from usable routes.

topics.question: How does mixing homes and shops change a neighborhood across a day?
topics.coverage: Map opening hours, deliveries, residences and noise on one block; include residents whose schedules differ from a commuter norm.

topics.question: What is the difference between density and overcrowding?
topics.coverage: Compare dwellings per hectare, people per room, public space and service capacity without treating a single density threshold as ideal.

topics.question: Who can use a public square when its design assumes everyone can stand and climb?
topics.coverage: Audit seating, gradients, shade, toilets and crossing times through different mobility needs; separate a design review from legal certification.

topics.question: How did Utrecht restore the Catharijnesingel waterway after a road conversion?
topics.coverage: Use city planning and opening records with dates; distinguish removal of one road section from a Europe-wide claim about highway demolition.

topics.question: Where does rain go after it lands on a paved neighborhood?
topics.coverage: Trace roof, road, drain, outfall and overflow in one catchment; contrast runoff reduction with moving water downstream.

topics.question: Why can two streets in the same city feel much hotter than each other?
topics.coverage: Compare surface material, shade, wind and measurement time; distinguish satellite surface temperature from pedestrian heat exposure.

topics.question: How does a city decide where its rubbish trucks should go first?
topics.coverage: Follow collection frequency, narrow streets, transfer sites and worker constraints; compare service reliability rather than shortest distance alone.

topics.question: What happens to a neighborhood when a bus route becomes reliable?
topics.coverage: Trace waiting time, transfers, operating budgets and reachable destinations; separate accessibility changes from speculative land-value claims.

topics.question: What can a zoning change permit without guaranteeing new homes?
topics.coverage: Follow one parcel through permitted use, finance, infrastructure and construction; distinguish legal capacity from completed supply.

topics.question: How can upgrading an informal settlement improve services without displacing residents?
topics.coverage: Compare tenure, utility access, rents and residents' participation in a bounded scheme; avoid assuming formalization has a single outcome.

topics.question: Who gets heard at a neighborhood planning meeting?
topics.coverage: Examine timing, language, childcare, landlord and tenant representation; compare meeting attendance with the affected population.

topics.question: How should a city compare a flood wall with leaving space for water?
topics.coverage: Define protected assets, residual risk, maintenance, downstream effects and relocation; keep climate scenarios explicit.

topics.question: How did a specified stair and access rule shape small apartment plans?
topics.coverage: Use a dated city or state code and built examples; distinguish one egress requirement from all causes of missing-middle housing or a universal ban.

topics.question: What do Singapore HDB statistics show about the resident population and tenure?
topics.coverage: Use dated official household and ownership tables; distinguish residents in HDB flats from citizens, owners, renters and an affordability outcome.

topics.question: Who pays to maintain a neighborhood street after its construction budget is spent?
topics.coverage: Trace capital grants, operating budgets, utilities, repairs, user fees and responsibility in one hypothetical street lifecycle; distinguish a maintenance backlog from the initial cost estimate.

# Cities & Urbanism Channel Master Topic Roadmap (Scratch to Advanced)
**Niche:** 111 Cities & Urbanism (Home_Living)  
**Channel Language:** English (YouTube)  
**Target Audience:** Urban Planners, Architects, Civil Geographers, City Dwellers, Civic Activists (Global)  
**Production Format:** 10-Minute Documentary Explainer Episodes (600s, 75 Fixed 8s Scenes)

## 1. Channel Progression Strategy

This curriculum organizes the core disciplines of Cities & Urbanism across four progressive tiers:
- **Tier 1: Urban Evolution, Street Grids & Human Scale (Beginner / Scratch)** — From ancient Jericho and Roman hippodamian grids to modern zoning laws, Jane Jacobs vs Robert Moses street philosophy, pedestrian ergonomics, and superblocks.
- **Tier 2: Infrastructure Systems, Densification & Public Space (Intermediate)** — Barcelona superilles, transit-oriented development (TOD), missing middle housing, urban heat island mitigation, and mixed-use commercial vitality.
- **Tier 3: Housing Crises, Gentrification & Adaptive Reuse (Upper Intermediate)** — Global affordability crunches, speculative property vacancy taxes, land value capture (Henry George), redlining historical impacts, and post-industrial brownfield remediation.
- **Tier 4: Megacities, Climate Resilience & The Future Metropolis (Advanced / Masterclass)** — Sponge cities against flash floods, delta urbanism (Tokyo/Rotterdam), master-planned capitals (Brasilia/Nusantara), smart sensor governance, and sustainable urban biophilia.

---

prior_initial_map.purpose: A starting subject map for a Cities & Urbanism YouTube channel. Categories organize concrete subtopics; each entry supplies an episode question, a research outline and a boundary for case selection. Counts follow the authored coverage, with no imposed topic maximum.

technical.requirements: Use the actual system documentation, a worked implementation and measurements. Identify inputs, outputs, constraints, tolerances, failure conditions and the limits of the example. Do not provide hazardous construction or unauthorized access procedures.
source_leads: official versioned product or standards documentation
test reports and drawings with clear provenance

community.requirements: Use consented participant accounts, local records and the community's own descriptions. Include differences of position, access and power; testimony is not a representative survey or clinical proof.
source_leads: field notes with method and consent documented

civic.requirements: Use the current official legal text, policy, procedure or public dataset for a specific jurisdiction and date. Distinguish written rules, implementation and lived access; give no personal legal or financial conclusion.
source_leads: official laws, rules and administrative guidance
audits, judgments and public service records
consented accounts from affected people and qualified specialists

handoff: Keep the BANK ID in notes. Refine the research question with an exact text edition, jurisdiction, population, product version, place, time range or clearly labeled fictional premise.
Inspect actual sources; no source was verified by generating this map. Apply the existing registry planning and idea readiness process before project creation.
Choose a current registered angle only after reading its niche-specific scope. This initial map has not checked or assigned angle plans for these entries.
Keep Q1-Q42, CAT defaults, project snapshots, output locations and production gates unchanged. Catalog counts are not production or publication counts.
Review neighboring banks for semantic overlap and follow the existing Phase 1 claim-ledger requirements. Add qualified review when required by the production contract.
prior_initial_map.coverage_limits: This initial map does not exhaust the niche, its regions, time periods, named case studies, texts, technical variants or disputed questions. It has not performed source-feasibility checks, semantic duplicate review of every pair, trend analysis, claim verification or episode production. Expand any category freely after identifying a real coverage gap; add categories where the subject requires them. Preserve existing IDs when refining wording and allocate new IDs only for genuinely new proposals.

open_coverage.next_step: Official MLIT material corrects the G-Cans outlet and unit; the existing imported BANK question remains preserved. Other planning outcomes, affordability, flood protection and project status claims need current site-specific primary records. No idea or episode was approved.
Compare less-visible regions, languages, participants and contrary cases within this niche; record substantive distinctions before adding another proposal.

coverage_mapping_review.method: Manual thematic cross-references to authored questions. A link is a navigation aid, not a claim that every aspect of a starter branch has been exhausted.
